note: First byte of fuzzer input controls maxarg (bits 0-5) and whether input is read from stdin (bit 6). Setting bit 6 makes the fuzzer redirect stdin to the temp file instead of passing the filename as an argument.
When use_stdin is false, the temp file path is appended to argv; when use_stdin is true, the file is redirected to stdin and no filename argument is added, so the decoder reads from stdin.
Invokes the FLAC tool main with the constructed argv. The decode path is reached when argv contains '-d' or the default mode decodes.
Calls decode_file() which sets up a DecoderSession and invokes the FLAC stream decoder on the attacker-controlled input.

A stack-allocated DecoderSession struct is created. Fields is_big_endian and is_unsigned_samples are only initialized when format==FORMAT_RAW; for WAVE/AIFF formats they remain uninitialized stack memory.
bps, channels, and sample_rate are initialized to 0. got_stream_info is set to false, meaning the decoder has not yet received a STREAMINFO metadata block.

code: init_status = FLAC__stream_decoder_init_file(decoder_session->decoder, strcmp(infilename, "-")? infilename : 0, write_callback, metadata_callback, error_callback, /*client_data=*/decoder_session);
note: Initializes the FLAC stream decoder with write_callback as the output callback. The decoder will call write_callback for each decoded frame.

code: const uint32_t bps = frame->header.bits_per_sample, channels = frame->header.channels;
note: Extracts bits-per-sample and channel count from the decoded frame header. These values come from the attacker-controlled FLAC frame.
Computes a shift value based on bps. For non-RAW output formats, if bps is not a multiple of 8, shift is set to 8-(bps%8). This shift is later added to bps to determine the output sample width.
When no STREAMINFO was received, decoder_session->bps is 0, so the else branch saves the frame's bps into decoder_session->bps. The frame's bps is attacker-controlled and may be any value 4-32.

code: else if(bps+shift == 16) { ... } else if(bps+shift == 24) { ... } else if(bps+shift == 8) { ... } else if(bps+shift == 32) { ... } else { FLAC__ASSERT(0); decoder_session->abort_flag = true; return FLAC__STREAM_DECODER_WRITE_STATUS_ABORT; }
note: The code checks bps+shift against 8, 16, 24, and 32. If bps is not a multiple of 8 (e.g., bps=12, shift=4, bps+shift=16), the value is accepted. However, when no STREAMINFO is present and bps is not a multiple of 8, the output conversion uses the uninitialized is_unsigned_samples field for FORMAT_RAW, or the shift causes the sample data to be read from uninitialized buffer positions.

code: FLAC__bool is_unsigned_samples = (decoder_session->format == FORMAT_AIFF || decoder_session->format == FORMAT_AIFF_C ? false : (decoder_session->format == FORMAT_WAVE || decoder_session->format == FORMAT_WAVE64 || decoder_session->format == FORMAT_RF64 ? bps<=8 : decoder_session->is_unsigned_samples));
note: For FORMAT_RAW output, decoder_session->is_unsigned_samples is read. This field is only initialized in flac__decode_file when format==FORMAT_RAW; for other formats it is uninitialized stack memory, leading to a use-of-uninitialized-value when the decoder processes a frame without STREAMINFO.

The converted sample data is written to the output file. When bps+shift does not match 8/16/24/32, the FLAC__ASSERT(0) is compiled out in fuzzing mode and the abort path is taken, but the uninitialized is_unsigned_samples value has already been used to select the conversion branch, causing MSAN to report a use-of-uninitialized-value.
